body: Chiang Mai's historic core is a nearly square ring of walls/moat. The temples inside **the Old City** are connected on foot and by short rides; to the east, **Tha Phae–Night Bazaar–Ping River** is the trading and evening axis; to the west, **the Nimman–university** area carries coffee, design and contemporary city life. Doi Suthep mountain, although it looks close on the map, is a separate half day with a winding climb.

The city centre isn't as big as Bangkok, but an "I'll walk everywhere" plan falls apart fast in the heat and on roads without pavements. You can walk from one end of the Old City to the other; don't put Nimman, the riverside and the bus/shopping areas on the same pedestrian loop. Combine the clusters by red songthaew, Grab or a hired driver.

What makes Chiang Mai special isn't a single monument but everyday detail: the neighbourhood temple with monks in the morning, the dried goods at Warorot, the shade of wooden Lanna roofs, the northern herbs at the evening market. Make room in your plan for aimless walking; but in the smoky period, reduce time spent outside according to air quality.
sections.heading: Understanding Chiang Mai: from the city inside the moat to the mountain

body: Because there are so many temples, it's easy for them all to look alike on the first day. Choosing a few examples with different architecture and roles in the city teaches you more.
sections.heading: Things to see: Lanna temples and living neighbourhoods

body: Wat Chedi Luang's great, partly ruined chedi shows the scale of the old capital; Wat Phra Singh's buildings show the Lanna decorative language. Link the two not as a straight dash down the main road but through small temple courtyards and wooden houses. The mornings are cooler and the rhythm of worship more visible.

At a temple entrance you need to cover your shoulders and knees, take off your shoes where marked and not point the soles of your feet at a sacred image when sitting. If there are monk-chat programmes, remember they're a space for mutual learning, not a tourist photo session. Female visitors shouldn't touch a monk directly; follow the method shown for passing objects.
subsections.heading: The Old City: Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Phra Singh and the side streets

body: With its tunnels and wooded grounds, Wat Umong is different from the central temples. Go early in the morning or on a cool afternoon; keep quiet in the tunnels. It can go in the same half day as the Nimman/university side, but walking along the main road isn't comfortable in every section.

Don't squeeze the nearby nature and reservoir areas in as compulsory stops from a social-media list. Chiang Mai's western edge slows down in evening traffic; if it clashes with the return from a Doi Suthep day, a short distance takes a long time.
subsections.heading: Wat Umong and the feel of the forest

body: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep is part of the city's identity. In clear weather the valley view is powerful; on a hazy or smoky day visibility may be limited. Going early in the morning is good for both heat and traffic. If the temple stairs are hard for you, ask on site about the current operating status of the available transport option.

Red songthaews may collect passengers around Chiang Mai Zoo/the mountain road; the vehicle sometimes waits to fill up. If you're going up by private car or app taxi, agree the return at the start, because finding an app car at the top isn't guaranteed. A scooter should only be considered by a licensed, experienced rider covered by insurance; bends, rain and downhill braking aren't a holiday experiment.
subsections.heading: Doi Suthep: as much the road plan as the view

body: **The Sunday Walking Street** sets up every Sunday around Ratchadamnoen and also appears as a weekly event in official tourism sources. Crafts, food and crowds come together; start near Tha Phae Gate and walk in before it gets busy. The Saturday Wua Lai market is on a separate street; don't mistake the two for the same-named night market.

**Warorot (Kad Luang)** is a local shopping market before it's a souvenir market: go by day for sai ua, nam prik, dried goods and textiles. **The Night Bazaar** is accessible every evening, but isn't the same as the weekend markets for authentic crafts and prices. Bargain with a smile; don't expect mass-produced factory prices from a small maker.
subsections.heading: Markets: which day, which character?

body: **The Old City** is the easiest choice for a first visit and temple walks. Its northern/eastern edges are close to restaurants and markets, its south-western part to quieter streets. On Sundays, road closures may affect taxi access; if your flight falls on a Sunday evening, ask the hotel about a transport plan.

**Nimman** offers contemporary cafés, bars, shopping and university energy. Some buildings near the aircraft approach path may be noisy; in room reviews, look not just at the overall score but at notes on planes and late-night music. Although it looks close to the Old City, you'll use transport rather than walking back and forth in the midday heat.

**Tha Phae–Night Bazaar–Ping River** offers access to dinner and markets, bigger hotel options and convenience for families. Not all the historic temples are on your doorstep, but transport is simple. **Santitham** can be more local and economical; check the night-time route back, the pavements and the hotel's surroundings on the map.

Choosing a mountain resort instead of a city hotel means a different holiday. If you plan to go down to the Old City every evening, transfer time and car costs wipe out the advantage. If you want both experiences, splitting it — say three nights in the city and two separate nights in the countryside — is more honest.
sections.heading: Where to stay? The Old City, Nimman and the riverside

body: Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX) is close to the centre; even so, rather than getting into a random vehicle in the arrivals hall, use the official taxi/transfer counter or the pickup point in the app. 24-hour designated pick-up and drop-off points between Grab and the airport have been officially announced. Follow the gate and terminal instructions in the app; don't look for the driver in the main traffic lane.

The red **songthaew** doesn't work like a fixed-stop city bus. The vehicles circulate and combine passengers going the same way; state your destination and agree the per-person fare before getting in. If you want a private route or a far destination, the price goes up. A driver making detours while there are other passengers inside may not be a scam; it's the nature of a shared system.

Grab makes prices visible in the city; Bolt coverage and waiting times can vary. In rain, market closures or airport rushes, finding a car takes longer. There's no metro/BTS in the city. As information on new electric buses/local lines can change, ask your hotel for the latest route, and don't tie your main plan to the map in a single travel blog.

Cycling can be pleasant in the Old City's quiet streets, but comfort drops fast on the ring road, at night and in rain. If you'll rent a scooter, you need a licence for the right motorcycle class plus an international driving permit, a helmet and policy coverage. Rather than leaving your passport as a deposit, ask about other forms of security; video every scratch when collecting the vehicle.
sections.heading: CNX airport and getting around the city

body: **Khao soi** is a balance of coconut-milk curry broth, boiled and crisp noodles, pickles, shallots and lime. There's no single "original" in the city; the broth's richness, the chilli oil and the noodle texture change from place to place. Trying a small/regular portion at two different places is more instructive than treating one queue as the ultimate truth.

**Sai ua** is a herby northern sausage; **nam prik noom** a roasted green chilli dip; **nam prik ong** a tomato and minced-pork dip; **gaeng hang lay** a pork curry layered with ginger and spices; **khanom jeen nam ngiao** a northern tomato noodle sauce. A khantoke show may serve some of these as a package, but also try the food at local eateries independent of the stage show.

Pork, fish sauce, shrimp paste and fermented ingredients are common in northern food. A dip or curry that looks vegetarian may contain animal products. The "jay" sign is an indicator close to the strict Thai vegetarian tradition, but it's not on every menu; with a serious allergy you need a card in Thai and confirmation from the kitchen.
sections.heading: What to eat in Chiang Mai? Get to know northern cuisine

body: **Doi Inthanon National Park** offers cool air, forest, waterfalls and hiking around Thailand's highest mountain. The round trip from the city and the distances within the park need a full day. The summit can be noticeably cooler than central Chiang Mai; in the rainy season there are slippery trails and visibility problems. Check park admission, trail/local guide and closing arrangements on official national park channels.

**Mae Kampong** is popular as a mountain village and a coffee/forest day. At weekends, the pressure of cars and visitors can exceed the village's scale; set off early and don't turn the road into a race between photo spots. Even if putting it on the same day as Doi Inthanon looks possible on the map, it's unnecessary driving.

In an elephant experience, the word "sanctuary" alone isn't an ethical credential. Riding, shows, compulsory contact off the chain and bathing programmes repeated with tourist groups are red flags. Observation from a distance, the animal being able to refuse contact, small groups, a transparent veterinary/care policy and verifiable rescue claims are better criteria. A guaranteed pose with a baby elephant or a programme points more to customer expectations than to animal welfare.
sections.heading: Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong and elephant experiences: not on the same day

body: The most critical calendar detail for Chiang Mai is **the risk of air pollution from February to April**. Agricultural burning, forest fires, dry air and the valley geography can worsen PM2.5; March is among the riskiest periods in most years, but the start and peak dates change every year. In spring 2026, the Thai government announced response visits and measures for fires, haze and PM2.5 in the north.

Don't look only at the sun icon in your weather app. Check official readings and health warnings such as Thailand's Pollution Control Department/Air4Thai before the trip and every morning. If values are bad, the Doi Suthep view, running, cycling and long outdoor days aren't a good idea; consider a suitable mask, filtered indoor spaces and changing your route.

November–January is the cool, dry and busy season. Yi Peng/Loy Krathong dates change with the lunar calendar; remember that releasing lanterns into the sky may only be possible in permitted areas and at permitted times, for city/airport safety reasons. Not every lantern event on social media is official or safe.
sections.heading: Smoke season: "the best weather" and "the cheapest month" aren't the same

body: Carry small THB notes for markets, songthaews and small eateries. PromptPay QR codes are everywhere, but most foreign travellers can't pay a standard code without a local bank account. Keep a card/ATM backup; read the rate and charges before accepting an ATM's own currency conversion.

At a market stall, don't assume a product is handmade just from a "handmade" label; if the same product appears identically at several stalls, it may be mass-produced. Politely ask where it comes from. Around temples, ask permission before photographing monks; don't turn the morning alms ritual into a flash-lit performance.

The most common route mistake is turning four nights into four full-day tours. Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong, an elephant centre and Chiang Rai are long days in different directions; if you do them all, you won't see Chiang Mai. Choose one countryside day and give the rest of your time to the city and the mountain temple.
sections.heading: Money, market etiquette and common mistakes

Un resort de montaña debe verse no como sustituto de la visita a la ciudad, sino como una experiencia aparte.
faqs.q: ¿Dónde alojarse en Chiang Mai?

faqs.a: El riesgo suele subir entre febrero y abril, y casi todos los años marzo es claramente malo; el inicio y el final exactos cambian cada año según el tiempo y los incendios. Consulta las mediciones oficiales de PM2.5 antes de comprar el billete y durante el viaje.
faqs.q: ¿Cuándo es la temporada del humo en Chiang Mai?

faqs.a: No. La Old City se recorre a pie; el songthaew y Grab cubren las excursiones principales. El scooter solo tiene sentido para un conductor con permiso válido para motos/permiso internacional, experiencia, casco y cobertura de seguro.
faqs.q: ¿Hace falta scooter en Chiang Mai?

faqs.a: Se puede usar el songthaew rojo que recoge pasajeros por la zona del zoo de Chiang Mai, un coche privado o una aplicación de coches. El vehículo compartido puede esperar a llenarse; deja clara a la ida la vuelta desde la cima.
faqs.q: ¿Cómo se va a Doi Suthep?

faqs.a: No mires el nombre «sanctuary», sino la práctica. En lugar de montar, espectáculos, baños obligados y contacto continuo, busca observación a distancia, que el animal pueda rechazar el contacto, grupos pequeños y una política veterinaria y de cuidados transparente.
faqs.q: ¿Cómo elegir un centro de elefantes ético en Chiang Mai?

faqs.a: El gran mercado peatonal en torno a Ratchadamnoen es el domingo. El de Wua Lai, el sábado, es otro mercado, y el Night Bazaar es otra zona, diaria. Verifica en el anuncio oficial vigente los horarios del evento y de los cortes de calles.
faqs.q: ¿Qué día es la Sunday Walking Street?

es.h1: Guía de viaje de Chiang Mai

itinerary.afternoon: Con el calor del mediodía, elige el que esté abierto entre Lanna Folklife y los museos de arte y cultura de la ciudad; luego camina hasta la puerta norte.
itinerary.evening: Si coincide el día, la Sunday Walking Street o el Saturday Wua Lai. Si no, comida del norte y un paseo tranquilo por las calles de la Old City.
itinerary.morning: Recorre temprano Wat Chedi Luang y Wat Phra Singh; deja tiempo para los pequeños templos y cafés de entre medias.
itinerary.title: Día 1: la Old City y la capa de Lanna

itinerary.afternoon: Almuerzo, galerías contemporáneas y café en Nimman. Baja el ritmo con el ruido de los aviones y el calor del mediodía.
itinerary.evening: Los alrededores de One Nimman o una casa de comidas local en Santitham; una noche más tranquila que no repita la del mercado.
itinerary.morning: Sube temprano a Doi Suthep; acuerda desde el principio el vehículo y la vuelta. Si la visibilidad es mala, dedica el tiempo a los detalles del templo.
itinerary.title: Día 2: Doi Suthep y Nimman

itinerary.afternoon: Ve despacio en la misma ruta; no añadas un segundo destino lejano. Sigue por los canales oficiales las normas del parque o del centro y el tiempo.
itinerary.evening: A la vuelta a la ciudad, un masaje o una comida sencilla cerca del hotel. Tras un largo trayecto, no hagas obligatorio el mercado nocturno.
itinerary.morning: Según el tiempo y tus intereses, ve solo a uno: Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong o un centro de elefantes centrado en la observación que hayas verificado de verdad.
itinerary.title: Día 3: la única ruta de campo que elijas

itinerary.afternoon: Prueba los productos del norte en el Warorot Market; camina hasta el mercado de flores de Ton Lamyai y las calles de Chang Moi.
itinerary.evening: Cena por el río Ping. Si vuelas al día siguiente, confirma con el hotel los cortes de calles del mercado y el vehículo al aeropuerto.
itinerary.morning: Visita Wat Umong a una hora tranquila; luego añade una breve parada por la universidad o la zona de Suan Dok.
itinerary.title: Día 4: Wat Umong, Warorot y el río

es.lede: Chiang Mai no es solo una versión más tranquila de Bangkok. La capital de Lanna dentro del foso, el moderno Nimman, los templos de montaña y la cocina del norte son capas distintas; un buen viaje, en lugar de amontonarlas en el mismo día, se adapta al ritmo de mañana y tarde de la ciudad.

places.known: Khao soi · Bib Gourmand Michelin 2026
places.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
places.tip: Verificado como Bib Gourmand en la página actual de Michelin; comprueba el mismo día si se agota pronto y los días de apertura.
places.why: Una buena entrada al plato emblemático de Chiang Mai, con un caldo de curry intenso, la textura de los fideos y sus acompañamientos. Una dirección sin pretensiones, de rotación rápida y centrada en el mediodía.

places.known: Cocina de Lanna en una casa histórica · Michelin Selected
places.name: Kiti Panit
places.tip: Plantéate reservar para la noche y el fin de semana; consulta el estatus actual en Michelin y en la web oficial del local.
places.why: Una buena respuesta para entender la comida del norte no solo con el cuenco callejero, sino con una carta más amplia y para compartir. El ambiente de la casa restaurada no le quita protagonismo a la comida.

places.known: Platos del norte de Tailandia para compartir
places.name: Huen Muan Jai
places.tip: Si sois dos, pregunta cuántos platos pedir; comparte las salsas picantes con arroz glutinoso y verduras.
places.why: Es más completo que los locales centrados en un solo plato para comparar en la misma mesa el nam prik, el sai ua, el gaeng hang lay y las hierbas de temporada.

places.known: Khao soi clásico en un barrio local
places.name: Khao Soi Mae Manee
places.tip: Planifica la vuelta; como los días de apertura y la hora del último servicio pueden cambiar, llama antes de ir.
places.why: Para quien quiere comparar un segundo estilo con el popular cuenco del centro. Por su ubicación más lejana, ve no solo por la foto, sino si de verdad te interesa el khao soi.

places.known: Pollo asado en espetón vertical y acompañamientos de Isan y del norte
places.name: SP Chicken
places.tip: Ve antes del pico del mediodía; di claramente el nivel de picante que quieres al pedir el som tam.
places.why: Un almuerzo rápido, para compartir y con carácter entre paseos por los templos. El pollo cobra sentido no solo, sino con som tam, arroz glutinoso y salsas de hierbas.

places.known: Sai ua, nam prik, productos secos y aperitivos locales
places.name: Warorot Market
places.tip: No compres para un viaje largo productos que necesiten cadena de frío; lleva billetes pequeños y una bolsa reutilizable.
places.why: En lugar de un solo restaurante, ves los ingredientes de la despensa del norte. Se va para probar allí mismo la salchicha fresca y comprar los productos envasados según las normas del vuelo y de aduanas.

es.practicalHeading: Lo que no debes ignorar antes de ir a Chiang Mai

practicalTips.body: De febrero a abril, no te fíes solo de la media histórica; mira los datos actuales de Air4Thai u oficiales. Un billete flexible y las condiciones de cancelación valen más que las vistas.
practicalTips.title: Consulta las PM2.5 antes de comprar el billete

practicalTips.body: Habla del destino y del precio por persona antes de subir. Como el vehículo compartido recoge a otros pasajeros, puede no seguir una ruta directa.
practicalTips.title: El songthaew no es una línea fija

practicalTips.body: Sigue la puerta de encuentro de la aplicación. En lugar de caminar al azar por el carril de llegadas, ve al punto de recogida oficial de 24 horas.
practicalTips.title: El punto de Grab en CNX está designado

practicalTips.body: El songthaew puede esperar a llenarse; la aplicación de coches no siempre muestra vehículos en la cima. A la ida, deja clara la opción de espera o de vuelta.
practicalTips.title: Resuelve antes la vuelta de Doi Suthep

practicalTips.body: En lugar de montar, espectáculos, baños obligados y posar con crías, busca observación en la que el animal pueda alejarse, grupos pequeños y una política de cuidados transparente.
practicalTips.title: Elige el centro de elefantes por su programa, no por su nombre

practicalTips.body: Los cortes de calles en torno a la Sunday Walking Street cambian la ruta de los vehículos. Planifica con el hotel el traslado a CNX del domingo por la tarde.
practicalTips.title: No hagas coincidir el domingo con el vuelo

practicalTips.body: Para la cima de Doi Inthanon y un día de lluvia en la montaña, lleva una capa fina de abrigo y un chubasquero; no salgas sin preparar mirando la temperatura de la ciudad.
practicalTips.title: En la montaña puede hacer más fresco que en la ciudad

practicalTips.body: Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong, Chiang Rai y el programa de elefantes son cuatro días largos distintos. Si no eliges uno, solo verás Chiang Mai por la noche.
practicalTips.title: No llenes todos los días de excursiones

relatedGuides.description: Al pasar de Chiang Mai al mar, no confundas el régimen de lluvias de octubre a diciembre de la isla con el de la costa del Andamán.

body: El núcleo histórico de Chiang Mai es un anillo de muralla y foso casi cuadrado. Los templos de la **Old City** se conectan a pie y con trayectos cortos; al este, **Tha Phae–Night Bazaar–río Ping** es el eje comercial y nocturno, y al oeste, la zona de **Nimman–universidad** reúne el café, el diseño y la vida urbana contemporánea. La montaña de Doi Suthep, aunque parezca cerca en el mapa, es una media jornada aparte con una subida llena de curvas.

El centro de la ciudad no es tan grande como Bangkok, pero el plan de «voy andando a todas partes» se deshace rápido con el calor y en calles sin acera. Se puede caminar de un extremo a otro de la Old City; no pongas Nimman, la orilla del río y las zonas de autobuses y compras en el mismo anillo peatonal. Combina los grupos con el songthaew rojo, Grab o un conductor contratado.

Lo que hace especial a Chiang Mai no es un solo monumento, sino el detalle cotidiano: el templo de barrio con monjes por la mañana, los productos secos de Warorot, la sombra de los tejados de madera de Lanna, las hierbas del norte en el mercado nocturno. Deja espacio en el programa para pasear sin rumbo; pero, en la época del humo, reduce el tiempo al aire libre según la calidad del aire.
sections.heading: Entender Chiang Mai: de la ciudad dentro del foso a la montaña

body: Como hay muchísimos templos, el primer día es fácil que todos parezcan iguales. Elegir unos pocos ejemplos con arquitectura y papel en la ciudad distintos enseña más.
sections.heading: Qué ver: templos de Lanna y barrios vivos

body: El gran chedi parcialmente en ruinas de Wat Chedi Luang muestra la escala de la antigua capital; los edificios de Wat Phra Singh, el lenguaje decorativo de Lanna. Únelos no con una carrera en línea recta por la calle principal, sino entre pequeños patios de templos y casas de madera. Por la mañana hace más fresco y el ritmo del culto es más visible.

Al entrar en el templo hay que cubrir hombros y rodillas, quitarse los zapatos donde se indique y, al sentarse, no dirigir las plantas de los pies hacia una imagen sagrada. Si hay programas de conversación con monjes, recuerda que no son una sesión de fotos turística, sino un espacio de aprendizaje mutuo. Las visitantes no deben tocar directamente a un monje; para darle un objeto, sigue el método que se indique.
subsections.heading: La Old City: Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Phra Singh y las callejuelas

body: Wat Umong, con sus túneles y su arboleda, es distinto de los templos del centro. Ve temprano o a media tarde, cuando refresca; guarda silencio en los túneles. Se puede poner en la misma media jornada que la zona de Nimman y la universidad, pero caminar por la carretera principal no es cómodo en todos los tramos.

No metas a presión las zonas naturales y los embalses cercanos como si fueran paradas obligatorias de una lista de redes sociales. El lado oeste de Chiang Mai se ralentiza con el tráfico de la tarde; si coincide con la vuelta del día de Doi Suthep, una distancia corta se alarga.
subsections.heading: Wat Umong y la sensación de bosque

body: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep forma parte de la identidad de la ciudad. Con el cielo despejado, las vistas del valle son impresionantes; en un día brumoso o con humo, la visibilidad puede ser limitada. Ir temprano es bueno tanto por el calor como por el tráfico. Si la escalinata del templo se te hace dura, pregunta allí si funciona la opción de transporte disponible.

Los songthaew rojos pueden recoger pasajeros en la zona del zoo de Chiang Mai y la carretera de la montaña; a veces el vehículo espera a llenarse. Si subes en coche privado o taxi de aplicación, acuerda la vuelta desde el principio, porque encontrar un coche de aplicación en la cima no está garantizado. El scooter solo se puede plantear para un conductor con permiso, experiencia y seguro que lo cubra; las curvas, la lluvia y los frenos de bajada no son para experimentar en vacaciones.
subsections.heading: Doi Suthep: el plan de la carretera tanto como las vistas

body: La **Sunday Walking Street** se monta cada domingo en torno a Ratchadamnoen y figura también como evento semanal en las fuentes oficiales de turismo. Llegan juntas la artesanía, la comida y la multitud; empieza cerca de la Tha Phae Gate y entra antes de que aumente la afluencia. El mercado del sábado de Wua Lai está en otra calle; no confundas los dos con el mercado nocturno del mismo nombre.

**Warorot (Kad Luang)** es, antes que de recuerdos turísticos, un mercado de compra local: ve de día por el sai ua, el nam prik, los productos secos y los tejidos. El **Night Bazaar** está disponible cada noche, pero no es igual que los mercados de fin de semana en autenticidad artesanal y precio. Regatea con una sonrisa; no esperes de un pequeño productor el precio de un producto de fábrica en serie.
subsections.heading: Mercados: ¿qué día y con qué carácter?

body: **La Old City** es la opción más fácil para una primera visita y los paseos de templos. Los bordes norte y este están más cerca de restaurantes y mercados; la parte suroeste, de calles más tranquilas. Los domingos, los cortes de calles pueden afectar al acceso en taxi; si tu vuelo cae el domingo por la tarde, pregunta al hotel por el plan del coche.

**Nimman** ofrece cafés contemporáneos, bares, compras y energía universitaria. En algunos edificios cercanos a la trayectoria de aproximación de los aviones puede haber ruido; en las opiniones de las habitaciones, no mires solo la puntuación general, sino las notas sobre aviones y música nocturna. Aunque parezca cerca de la Old City, con el calor del mediodía usarás un vehículo en lugar de caminar todo el rato.

**Tha Phae–Night Bazaar–río Ping** ofrece acceso para cenar y a los mercados, opciones de hoteles más grandes y comodidad para familias. No tienes todos los templos históricos en la puerta, pero el transporte es sencillo. **Santitham** puede ser más local y económico; estudia en el mapa la ruta de vuelta nocturna, las aceras y el entorno del hotel.

Elegir un resort de montaña en lugar de un hotel en la ciudad son otras vacaciones. Si piensas bajar cada noche a la Old City, el tiempo de traslado y el coste del vehículo borran la ventaja. Si quieres las dos experiencias, es más honesto dividirlas, por ejemplo, en tres noches en la ciudad y dos aparte en el campo.
sections.heading: ¿Dónde alojarse? La Old City, Nimman y la orilla del río

body: El Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX) está cerca del centro; aun así, en lugar de subir a un coche al azar en la sala de llegadas, usa el mostrador oficial de taxis/traslados o el punto de encuentro de la aplicación. Se han anunciado oficialmente puntos de recogida y bajada de Grab en el aeropuerto designados las 24 horas. Sigue las instrucciones de puerta y terminal de la aplicación; no busques al conductor en el carril principal del tráfico.

El **songthaew** rojo no funciona como un autobús urbano con paradas fijas. Los vehículos circulan y juntan a los pasajeros que van en la misma dirección; di tu destino y deja claro el precio por persona antes de subir. Si quieres una ruta privada o un destino lejano, el precio sube. Que el conductor dé un rodeo cuando hay otros pasajeros puede no ser una estafa, sino la naturaleza del sistema compartido.

Grab hace visible el precio dentro de la ciudad; la cobertura y la espera de Bolt pueden variar. Con lluvia, cierres por mercado o mucha afluencia en el aeropuerto, encontrar coche tarda más. En la ciudad no hay metro ni BTS. Como la información sobre los nuevos autobuses eléctricos y las líneas locales puede cambiar, pregunta en tu hotel la ruta más actual y no ates el plan principal al mapa de un solo blog de viajes.

La bicicleta puede ser agradable por las calles tranquilas de la Old City, pero en la ronda, de noche y con lluvia la comodidad cae rápido. Si vas a alquilar un scooter, hacen falta un permiso adecuado para la clase de moto y un permiso internacional, casco y cobertura de la póliza. En lugar de dejar el pasaporte como depósito, pregunta por otra garantía; al recoger el vehículo, graba en vídeo todos los arañazos.
sections.heading: El aeropuerto CNX y el transporte urbano

body: El **khao soi** es un equilibrio de caldo de curry con leche de coco, fideos cocidos y crujientes, encurtidos, chalota y lima. En la ciudad no hay un único «original»; la intensidad del caldo, el aceite picante y la textura de los fideos cambian de una dirección a otra. Probar una ración pequeña o normal en dos sitios distintos enseña más que tomar una cola como verdad definitiva.

El **sai ua** es una salchicha del norte con hierbas; el **nam prik noom**, una pasta de pimientos verdes asados; el **nam prik ong**, una salsa para mojar de tomate y carne picada; el **gaeng hang lay**, un curry de cerdo con capas de jengibre y especias, y el **khanom jeen nam ngiao**, una salsa de fideos del norte con tomate. El espectáculo de khantoke puede ofrecer algunos de estos platos en un paquete, pero pruébalos también en casas de comidas locales, al margen del espectáculo.

En los platos del norte son habituales el cerdo, la salsa de pescado, la pasta de gambas y los ingredientes fermentados. Una salsa o un curry que parecen vegetarianos pueden llevar ingredientes animales. La marca «jay» indica algo cercano a la estricta tradición vegetariana tailandesa, pero no aparece en todas las cartas; con alergias graves hacen falta una tarjeta en tailandés y la confirmación de la cocina.
sections.heading: ¿Qué comer en Chiang Mai? Conoce la cocina del norte

body: El **Doi Inthanon National Park** ofrece, en torno a la montaña más alta de Tailandia, aire fresco, bosque, cascadas y caminatas. La ida y vuelta desde la ciudad y las distancias dentro del parque exigen un día completo. En la cima puede hacer bastante más fresco que en el centro de Chiang Mai; en la temporada de lluvias hay senderos resbaladizos y problemas de visibilidad. Consulta en los canales oficiales del parque nacional la entrada, los senderos y guías locales y el horario de cierre.

**Mae Kampong** es popular como pueblo de montaña y día de café y bosque. Los fines de semana, la presión de coches y visitantes puede superar la escala del pueblo; sal temprano y no conviertas el camino en una carrera entre puntos para fotos. Ponerlo el mismo día que Doi Inthanon, aunque en el mapa parezca posible, es conducir de forma innecesaria.

En una experiencia con elefantes, la palabra «sanctuary» no es por sí sola un certificado ético. Montar, los espectáculos, el contacto obligado fuera de la cadena y los programas de baño repetidos con grupos de turistas son señales de alarma. Son mejores criterios la observación a distancia, que el animal pueda rechazar el contacto, los grupos pequeños, una política veterinaria y de cuidados transparente y que las afirmaciones de rescate sean verificables. La garantía de posar con una cría o de un programa fijo apunta más a las expectativas del cliente que al bienestar animal.
sections.heading: Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong y la experiencia con elefantes: no el mismo día

body: El detalle más crítico del calendario de Chiang Mai es **el riesgo de contaminación del aire de febrero a abril**. Las quemas agrícolas, los incendios forestales, el aire seco y la geografía del valle pueden agravar las PM2.5; marzo es casi todos los años uno de los periodos de más riesgo, pero las fechas de inicio y del pico cambian cada año. En la primavera de 2026, el Gobierno de Tailandia anunció visitas de intervención y medidas contra los incendios, la bruma y las PM2.5 en el norte.

No mires solo el icono del sol en la aplicación del tiempo. Consulta antes del viaje y cada mañana las mediciones oficiales y los avisos sanitarios, como los del Pollution Control Department/Air4Thai de Tailandia. Si los valores son malos, las vistas de Doi Suthep, correr, ir en bici y un día largo al aire libre no son buena idea; piensa en una mascarilla adecuada, interiores con filtro y un cambio de ruta.

De noviembre a enero es la temporada fresca, seca y concurrida. Las fechas de Yi Peng/Loy Krathong cambian según el calendario lunar; no olvides que soltar farolillos al cielo, por la seguridad de la ciudad y del aeropuerto, puede estar permitido solo en zonas y horas autorizadas. No todos los eventos de farolillos de las redes sociales son oficiales ni seguros.
sections.heading: La temporada del humo: «el mejor tiempo» y «el mes más barato» no son lo mismo

body: Para el mercado, el songthaew y las pequeñas casas de comidas, lleva billetes pequeños de THB. El QR de PromptPay se ve por todas partes, pero la mayoría de los viajeros extranjeros no pueden pagar el código estándar sin una cuenta bancaria local. Mantén la tarjeta o el cajero como reserva; antes de aceptar la conversión de moneda del propio cajero, lee el tipo de cambio y la comisión.

En un puesto del mercado, no des por hecho que un producto es artesanal solo por la etiqueta «handmade»; si el mismo producto aparece idéntico en varios puestos, puede ser de fabricación en serie. Pregunta con amabilidad por su origen. Junto a los templos, pide permiso antes de fotografiar a un monje; no conviertas el ritual de ofrendas de la mañana en una actuación con flash.

El error de ruta más frecuente es convertir cuatro noches en cuatro excursiones de día completo. Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong, un centro de elefantes y Chiang Rai son días largos en direcciones distintas; si los haces todos, no verás Chiang Mai. Elige un día de campo y dedica el resto del tiempo a la ciudad y al templo de la montaña.

faqs.a: Old City, Doi Suthep, pazarlar ve bir kırsal gün için 4 tam gün idealdir. Üç günde şehir ile yalnız bir dış rotayı dengeli görebilirsiniz. Chiang Rai'yi aynı süreye eklemek geziyi büyük ölçüde araç yolculuğuna çevirir.
faqs.q: Chiang Mai kaç günde gezilir?

faqs.a: Tapınak ve ilk ziyaret için Old City; çağdaş yemek/kahve ve gece hayatı için Nimman; büyük otel, pazar ve nehir için Tha Phae–Night Bazaar hattı uygundur. Dağ resortu şehir gezisinin yerine değil ayrı bir deneyim olarak düşünülmeli.
faqs.q: Chiang Mai'de nerede kalınır?

faqs.a: Risk genellikle şubat–nisan arasında yükselir ve çoğu yıl mart belirgin biçimde kötüdür; kesin başlangıç/bitiş her yıl hava ve yangınlara göre değişir. Bilet öncesi ve gezi sırasında resmî PM2.5 ölçümlerini kontrol edin.
faqs.q: Chiang Mai duman sezonu ne zaman?

faqs.a: Hayır. Old City yürünebilir; songthaew ve Grab ana gezileri karşılar. Scooter yalnız motosiklet yetkili ehliyet/uluslararası belge, deneyim, kask ve sigorta kapsamı olan sürücü için anlamlıdır.
faqs.q: Chiang Mai'de scooter gerekli mi?

faqs.a: Chiang Mai Zoo çevresinden yolcu toplayan kırmızı songthaew, özel araç veya çağırma uygulaması kullanılabilir. Paylaşımlı araç dolmayı bekleyebilir; zirveden dönüşü gidişte netleştirin.
faqs.q: Doi Suthep'e nasıl gidilir?

faqs.a: 'Sanctuary' adına değil uygulamaya bakın. Binme, gösteri, zorunlu banyo ve sürekli dokunma yerine uzak gözlem, hayvanın teması reddedebilmesi, küçük grup ve şeffaf veteriner/bakım politikası arayın.
faqs.q: Chiang Mai'de etik fil merkezi nasıl seçilir?

faqs.a: Ratchadamnoen çevresindeki büyük yürüyüş pazarı pazar günüdür. Cumartesi Wua Lai ayrı pazardır; Night Bazaar ise başka, günlük bir bölgedir. Etkinlik ve yol kapanışı saatlerini güncel resmî duyurudan doğrulayın.
faqs.q: Sunday Walking Street hangi gün?

itinerary.afternoon: Öğle sıcağında Lanna Folklife veya şehir sanat/kültür müzelerinden güncel açık olanı seçin; sonra kuzey kapısına yürüyün.
itinerary.evening: Güne denk geliyorsa Sunday Walking Street veya Saturday Wua Lai. Değilse Old City'de kuzey yemeği ve sakin sokak yürüyüşü.
itinerary.morning: Wat Chedi Luang ve Wat Phra Singh'i erken gezin; aradaki küçük tapınak ve kahvelere zaman bırakın.
itinerary.title: 1. Gün — Old City ve Lanna katmanı

itinerary.afternoon: Nimman'da öğle yemeği, çağdaş galeriler ve kahve. Uçuş hattı gürültüsü ile öğle sıcaklığında tempoyu düşürün.
itinerary.evening: One Nimman çevresi veya Santitham'da yerel lokanta; pazar gecesini tekrar etmeyen daha sakin bir akşam.
itinerary.morning: Doi Suthep'e erken çıkın; araç ve dönüş anlaşmasını baştan yapın. Görüş kötüyse zamanı tapınağın ayrıntılarına ayırın.
itinerary.title: 2. Gün — Doi Suthep ve Nimman

itinerary.afternoon: Aynı rotada yavaşlayın; ikinci uzak hedef eklemeyin. Park/tesis kuralları ve hava durumunu resmî kanaldan izleyin.
itinerary.evening: Şehre dönüşte masaj veya otelinize yakın sade yemek. Uzun sürüşten sonra gece pazarını zorunlu tutmayın.
itinerary.morning: Hava ve ilginize göre Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong ya da gerçekten doğruladığınız gözlem odaklı fil merkezinden yalnız birine gidin.
itinerary.title: 3. Gün — Seçtiğiniz tek kırsal rota

itinerary.afternoon: Warorot Market'ta kuzey ürünlerini tadın; Ton Lamyai çiçek pazarı ve Chang Moi sokaklarına yürüyün.
itinerary.evening: Ping Nehri çevresinde akşam yemeği. Ertesi gün uçuş varsa pazar yol kapanışı ve havaalanı aracını otelle teyit edin.
itinerary.morning: Wat Umong'u sessiz saatte gezin; sonra üniversite çevresi veya Suan Dok tarafına kısa durak ekleyin.
itinerary.title: 4. Gün — Wat Umong, Warorot ve nehir

body: Chiang Mai'nin tarihî çekirdeği kareye yakın sur/hendek halkasıdır. **Old City** içindeki tapınaklar yürüyerek ve kısa araçlarla bağlanır; doğudaki **Tha Phae–Night Bazaar–Ping Nehri** ticaret ve akşam aksıdır; batıdaki **Nimman–üniversite** bölgesi kahve, tasarım ve çağdaş şehir hayatını taşır. Doi Suthep dağı ise haritada yakın görünse de virajlı tırmanışla ayrı bir yarım gündür.

Şehir merkezi Bangkok kadar büyük değildir ama 'her yere yürürüm' planı sıcakta ve kaldırımsız yollarda hızla dağılır. Old City'nin bir ucundan diğerine yürünebilir; Nimman, nehir kıyısı ve otobüs/alışveriş bölgelerini aynı yaya halkasına koymayın. Kırmızı songthaew, Grab veya kiralık şoförle kümeleri birleştirin.

Chiang Mai'yi özel yapan şey tek bir anıt değil, gündelik ayrıntıdır: sabah keşişlerin olduğu mahalle tapınağı, Warorot'taki kurutulmuş ürünler, ahşap Lanna çatılarının gölgesi, akşam pazarında kuzey otları. Programda amaçsız yürüyüşe yer açın; ancak dumanlı dönemde dışarıda geçirilen süreyi hava kalitesine göre azaltın.
sections.heading: Chiang Mai'yi anlamak: hendek içi şehirden dağa

body: Tapınak sayısı yüksek olduğu için ilk günde hepsinin birbirine benzemesi kolaydır. Mimarisi ve şehirdeki rolü farklı birkaç örneği seçmek daha çok şey öğretir.
sections.heading: Gezilecek yerler: Lanna tapınakları ve yaşayan mahalleler

body: Wat Chedi Luang'ın kısmen yıkık büyük chedisi eski başkentin ölçeğini; Wat Phra Singh'in yapıları Lanna süsleme dilini gösterir. İkisini ana caddeden düz koşu gibi değil, küçük tapınak avluları ve ahşap evlerin arasından bağlayın. Sabah saatleri daha serin ve ibadet ritmi daha görünürdür.

Tapınak girişinde omuz ve diz örtmek, ayakkabıyı işaretli yerde çıkarmak ve otururken ayak tabanını kutsal imgeye yöneltmemek gerekir. Rahiple sohbet programları varsa bunun turistik fotoğraf seansı değil karşılıklı öğrenme alanı olduğunu unutmayın. Kadın ziyaretçiler keşişe doğrudan temas etmemelidir; nesne aktarımında gösterilen yöntemi izleyin.
subsections.heading: Old City: Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Phra Singh ve ara sokaklar

body: Wat Umong, tünelleri ve ağaçlık alanıyla merkez tapınaklarından farklıdır. Sabah erken veya serin öğleden sonra gidin; tünellerde sessizliği koruyun. Nimman/üniversite tarafıyla aynı yarım güne konabilir, fakat ana yoldan yürümek her bölümde rahat değildir.

Yakındaki doğa ve rezervuar alanlarını sosyal medya listesindeki zorunlu duraklar gibi sıkıştırmayın. Chiang Mai'nin batı kıyısı akşam trafiğinde yavaşlar; Doi Suthep gününden dönüşle çakışırsa kısa mesafe uzun sürer.
subsections.heading: Wat Umong ve orman hissi

body: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep şehir kimliğinin parçasıdır. Açık havada vadi manzarası güçlüdür; puslu veya dumanlı günde görüş sınırlanabilir. Sabah erken gitmek hem sıcak hem trafik açısından iyidir. Tapınağın merdiveni zor gelirse mevcut ulaşım seçeneğinin güncel çalışma durumunu yerinde sorun.

Kırmızı songthaew'ler Chiang Mai Zoo/dağ yolu çevresinde yolcu toplayabilir; araç bazen dolmayı bekler. Özel araç veya uygulama taksisiyle çıkıyorsanız dönüşü baştan konuşun, çünkü zirvede uygulama aracı bulmak garanti değildir. Scooter yalnız ehliyetli, deneyimli ve sigortası kapsayan sürücü için düşünülebilir; viraj, yağmur ve iniş frenleri tatil denemesi değildir.
subsections.heading: Doi Suthep: manzara kadar yol planı

body: **Sunday Walking Street**, her pazar Ratchadamnoen çevresinde kurulur ve resmî turizm kaynaklarında da haftalık etkinlik olarak yer alır. El işi, yiyecek ve kalabalık birlikte gelir; Tha Phae Gate'e yakın başlayıp yoğunluk artmadan içeri yürüyün. Cumartesi Wua Lai pazarı ayrı caddededir; ikisini aynı isimli gece pazarı sanmayın.

**Warorot (Kad Luang)** turist hediyeliğinden önce yerel alışveriş pazarıdır: sai ua, nam prik, kurutulmuş ürün ve tekstil için gündüz gidin. **Night Bazaar** her akşam erişilebilir ama el işi özgünlüğü ve fiyat açısından hafta sonu pazarlarıyla aynı değildir. Pazarlığı gülümseyerek yapın; küçük üreticide toplu fabrika malı fiyatı beklemeyin.
subsections.heading: Pazarlar: hangi gün, hangi karakter?

body: **Old City**, ilk ziyaret ve tapınak yürüyüşleri için en kolay seçimdir. Kuzey/doğu kenarları restoran ve pazar erişimine, güneybatı bölümü daha sakin sokaklara yakındır. Pazar günleri yol kapanışı taksi erişimini etkileyebilir; uçuşunuz pazar akşamına denk geliyorsa otelden araç planını sorun.

**Nimman**, çağdaş kahveler, barlar, alışveriş ve üniversite enerjisi sunar. Uçak yaklaşma hattına yakın bazı binalarda gürültü olabilir; oda yorumlarında yalnız genel puana değil uçak ve gece müziği notlarına bakın. Old City'ye yakın görünse de öğle sıcağında sürekli yürümek yerine araç kullanırsınız.

**Tha Phae–Night Bazaar–Ping Nehri**, akşam yemeği ve pazar erişimi, daha büyük otel seçenekleri ve aileler için kolaylık sunar. Tarihî tapınakların hepsi kapıda değildir ama ulaşım basittir. **Santitham** daha yerel ve ekonomik olabilir; gece dönüş rotasını, kaldırımı ve otel çevresini haritada inceleyin.

Dağ resortunu şehir oteli yerine seçmek farklı tatil demektir. Her akşam Old City'ye inmeyi planlıyorsanız transfer süresi ve araç maliyeti avantajı siler. İki deneyim istiyorsanız şehirde üç gece, kırsalda ayrı iki gece gibi bölmek daha dürüsttür.
sections.heading: Nerede kalınır? Old City, Nimman ve nehir kıyısı

body: Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX) merkeze yakındır; yine de geliş salonunda rastgele araca binmek yerine resmî taksi/transfer bankosu veya uygulamadaki karşılama noktasını kullanın. Grab ile havalimanı arasında 24 saat belirlenmiş alma–bırakma noktaları resmî olarak duyuruldu. Uygulamadaki kapı ve terminal talimatını takip edin; sürücüyü ana trafik şeridinde aramayın.

Kırmızı **songthaew** sabit duraklı şehir otobüsü gibi işlemez. Araçlar dolaşır, aynı yöndeki yolcuları birleştirir; hedefi söyleyip kişi başı ücreti binmeden netleştirin. Özel rota veya uzak hedef isterseniz fiyat yükselir. Aracın içinde diğer yolcular varken sürücünün dolambaç yapması dolandırıcılık olmayabilir, paylaşımlı sistemin doğasıdır.

Grab şehir içinde fiyatı görünür kılar; Bolt kapsaması ve bekleme süresi değişebilir. Yağmur, pazar kapanışı veya havaalanı yoğunluğunda araç bulma süresi uzar. Şehirde metro/BTS yoktur. Yeni elektrikli otobüs/yerel hat bilgileri değişebildiğinden otelinize en güncel rotayı sorun, ana planı tek bir seyahat blogundaki haritaya bağlamayın.

Bisiklet Old City'nin sakin sokaklarında keyifli olabilir fakat çevre yolunda, gece ve yağmurda konfor hızla düşer. Scooter kiralayacaksanız motosiklet sınıfına uygun ehliyet ve uluslararası sürücü belgesi, kask ve poliçe kapsamı gerekir. Pasaportu depozito bırakmak yerine başka teminat seçeneğini sorun; aracı teslim alırken tüm çizikleri videoya kaydedin.
sections.heading: CNX havalimanı ve şehir içi ulaşım

body: **Khao soi**, Hindistan cevizi sütlü körili et suyu, haşlanmış ve çıtır erişte, turşu, arpacık soğanı ve lime dengesidir. Şehirde tek bir 'orijinal' yoktur; et suyu yoğunluğu, acı yağ ve erişte dokusu adresten adrese değişir. İki farklı yerde küçük/normal porsiyon denemek, bir kuyruğu nihai hakikat saymaktan daha öğreticidir.

**Sai ua** otlu kuzey sosisi; **nam prik noom** közlenmiş yeşil biber ezmesi; **nam prik ong** domatesli kıymalı dip; **gaeng hang lay** zencefil ve baharat katmanlı domuz körisi; **khanom jeen nam ngiao** domatesli kuzey erişte sosudur. Kantoke gösterisi bu yemeklerin bazılarını paket halinde sunabilir fakat yemeği sahne gösterisinden bağımsız yerel lokantalarda da deneyin.

Kuzey yemeklerinde domuz eti, balık sosu, karides ezmesi ve fermente malzeme yaygındır. Vejetaryen görünen dip veya köri hayvansal içerik taşıyabilir. 'Jay' işareti katı Tayland vejetaryen geleneğine yakın bir gösterge olsa da her menüde bulunmaz; ciddi alerjide Tayca kart ve mutfak teyidi gerekir.
sections.heading: Chiang Mai'de ne yenir? Kuzey mutfağını tanıyın

body: **Doi Inthanon National Park** Tayland'ın en yüksek dağı çevresinde serin hava, orman, şelale ve yürüyüş sunar. Şehirden gidiş–dönüş ve park içi mesafeler tam gün gerektirir. Zirvede Chiang Mai merkezinden belirgin daha serin olabilir; yağmur döneminde kaygan patika ve görüş sorunu vardır. Park giriş, parkur/yerel rehber ve kapanış düzenini resmî millî park kanallarından kontrol edin.

**Mae Kampong** dağ köyü ve kahve/orman günü olarak popülerdir. Hafta sonu araç ve ziyaretçi baskısı köyün ölçeğini aşabilir; erken çıkın, yolu yalnız fotoğraf noktaları arasında yarışa çevirmeyin. Doi Inthanon ile aynı güne koymak harita üzerinde mümkün görünse bile gereksiz sürüştür.

Fil deneyiminde 'sanctuary' kelimesi tek başına etik belge değildir. Binme, gösteri, zincir dışı zorunlu temas ve turist gruplarıyla tekrarlanan banyo programı kırmızı bayraktır. Uzaktan gözlem, hayvanın teması reddedebilmesi, küçük grup, şeffaf veteriner/bakım politikası ve kurtarma iddialarının doğrulanabilirliği daha iyi ölçütlerdir. Yavruyla poz veya program garantisi, hayvan refahından çok müşteri beklentisine işaret eder.
sections.heading: Doi Inthanon, Mae Kampong ve fil deneyimi: aynı gün değil

body: Chiang Mai için takvimdeki en kritik ayrıntı **şubat–nisan hava kirliliği riskidir**. Tarımsal yakma, orman yangını, kuru hava ve vadi coğrafyası PM2.5'i ağırlaştırabilir; mart çoğu yıl en riskli dönemlerden biridir ama başlangıç ve zirve tarihi her yıl değişir. 2026 ilkbaharında Tayland hükûmeti kuzeyde yangın, pus ve PM2.5 için müdahale ziyaretleri ve önlemler duyurdu.

Yalnız hava durumu uygulamasındaki güneş simgesine bakmayın. Tayland Pollution Control Department/Air4Thai gibi resmî ölçümleri ve sağlık uyarılarını seyahatten önce ve her sabah kontrol edin. Değerler kötüyse Doi Suthep manzarası, koşu, bisiklet ve uzun dış mekân günü iyi fikir değildir; uygun maske, filtreli iç mekân ve rota değişikliği düşünün.

Kasım–ocak serin, kuru ve yoğun sezondur. Yi Peng/Loy Krathong tarihleri ay takvimine göre değişir; gökyüzüne fener bırakmanın şehir/havalimanı güvenliği nedeniyle yalnız izinli alan ve saatlerde mümkün olabileceğini unutmayın. Sosyal medyadaki her fener etkinliği resmî veya güvenli değildir.

faqs.a: 5 days is comfortable for a beach base, the Old Town, a boat day and a southern island route. It can be done in four; in the monsoon season the buffer for cancellations shrinks. Two or three days only suit your chosen coast or a transit stop.
faqs.q: How many days do you need for Phuket?

faqs.a: Patong for nightlife and convenience; Kata/Karon for a balanced beach; Bang Tao for resorts and a long beach; Rawai–Nai Harn for a quiet south/long stays; the Old Town for food and culture. Mai Khao/Nai Yang can be considered for proximity to the airport.
faqs.q: Which area should I stay in, in Phuket?

faqs.a: An official taxi/hotel transfer/Grab is door to door; the Phuket Smart Bus is the economical option along the west coast. The bus stops a lot and may not reach your hotel's door; check the current stop and last service with the official operator.
faqs.q: How do you get from Phuket airport to Patong, Kata or Rawai?

faqs.a: Not if you stay in one area and do one or two tours. On a scattered island route, a car/driver can be useful. A scooter should only be considered with a motorcycle licence and IDP, experience, a helmet and insurance cover.
faqs.q: Do you need a car or scooter in Phuket?

faqs.a: November–April usually brings calmer seas; in the May–October monsoon, waves, rip currents and boat cancellations can increase. The weather varies from year to year; TMD marine warnings and beach flags are decisive.
faqs.q: Which month should you go to Phuket?

faqs.a: With limited time, a licensed tour is easy; staying overnight on Phi Phi for an island feel outside the crowded hours is a different experience. Leave room for ferry/boat cancellations and don't tie your return to the same day as an international flight.
faqs.q: From Phuket to Phi Phi: a day trip or an overnight stay?

faqs.a: No. The Old Town is inland in the south-east of the island, and you can't walk to a swimming beach. Plan it as a food/culture base or a one-day route; you need transport for beach days.
faqs.q: Is Phuket Old Town close to the beach?

itinerary.afternoon: Spend the heat of the day with a pool/shade break. If there's a nearby second cove, make that the day's one short transfer; don't cross the island.
itinerary.evening: A beachside dinner in Kata/Karon, a neighbourhood/resort choice in Bang Tao, or a night plan in Patong whose rules you know.
itinerary.morning: Get to know the area around your hotel and your main beach on foot; find the lifeguard flags, a convenience store and the real Smart Bus stop.
itinerary.title: Day 1 — A slow start on your chosen coast

itinerary.afternoon: A museum/shophouse visit and a shared Phuket lunch. If it's a Sunday, arrange your transport back around the road closures.
itinerary.evening: The Lard Yai Sunday Walking Street if the day falls right; if not, Go Benz or another neighbourhood dinner in the Old Town.
itinerary.morning: Old Town façades, Chinese-Thai temples and a local breakfast. Before midday the streets are more photogenic and cooler.
itinerary.title: Day 2 — The Old Town and Phuket food

itinerary.afternoon: Swimming/kayaking/snorkelling on the same tour. Follow life jacket and park rules; don't step on coral or feed the fish.
itinerary.evening: Keep the evening you get back close to your hotel. Don't plan a long taxi ride and a nightclub after a speedboat.
itinerary.morning: If the weather allows, take one of the Phi Phi, Phang Nga or Racha tours according to your interests. Confirm the pier and pickup time the night before.
itinerary.title: Day 3 — A single sea route

itinerary.afternoon: The Rawai–Nai Harn line and a local lunch in Chalong/Pa Lai. Don't mistake Rawai for a swimming beach.
itinerary.evening: Sunset on a southern beach of your choice instead of the Promthep crowds; a safe return in a car with driver.
itinerary.morning: Wat Chalong; if official access is open, the Big Buddha area under current conditions. Prepare suitable clothing and sun protection.
itinerary.title: Day 4 — Southern Phuket

itinerary.afternoon: If it's rainy, an Old Town museum or a cooking class; if it's clear, viewpoints and a short neighbourhood route. Don't go to a far-off island on the last day.
itinerary.evening: Sort out your luggage and HKT transfer; depending on your flight time, confirm the Smart Bus's last service or a private car booking.
itinerary.morning: Leave room for a cancelled boat day; if the weather is good, swim at your own beach. With a red flag, choose the pool/spa.
itinerary.title: Day 5 — A weather buffer and your own island

en.lede: Phuket isn't a beach town but a large island province where travelling from north to south can take hours depending on traffic. The quality of your holiday depends most not on which hotel, but on which coast you choose as a base and for what purpose.

body: Phuket's airport is in the north, Phuket Old Town in the south-east, and most of the popular beaches on the west coast. Patong to Kata looks short but involves a hill, bends and traffic; going down from the airport to Rawai means crossing almost the whole island. Build your daily plan not as "in Phuket" but as **north-west, central west, south and Old Town**.

Taking a taxi to a different beach every day on the same holiday isn't freedom; it's a transport budget and lost time. Choose one priority — swimming, nightlife, a holiday with children, local food or boat trips — and set your base accordingly. Staying in the Old Town and going to the beach every day, or staying in Mai Khao and going down to Patong every evening, are two examples of the wrong extremes.

Phuket's coastal photos don't exist independently of weather and tides. The Andaman Sea can be rougher and more changeable from May to October. A beach being swimmable in the morning doesn't mean the currents will stay safe in the afternoon; lifeguard flags and announcements are more current than map reviews.
sections.heading: Understanding Phuket: a big island with very different coasts

body: **Patong** has the busiest nightlife, shopping, tour sellers and transport options. Practical for travellers without a car; it can be noisy and commercial for anyone looking for a quiet beach holiday. Someone who wants to be near Bangla Road and a family who wants to sleep shouldn't choose the same Patong hotel; read reviews about the street and noise.

**Kata** is strong for a beach–restaurant balance in swimming season and a mid-sized holiday. **Karon** feels like a longer, more open beach; a hotel "opposite" the beach sometimes means crossing a busy road. The two areas are close, but hilly connecting roads don't make walking easy everywhere.

**Bang Tao–Cherngtalay–Laguna** offers a long beach and an ecosystem of beach clubs, villas and resorts. It's closer to the airport in the north than Patong/Kata, and far from the Old Town and southern piers. The car/app budget is high and people stay inside their properties a lot. Nightlife isn't Patong but a more scattered line of restaurants and clubs.

**Kamala** can be a middle way, calmer than Patong and more compact than Bang Tao. Not every end of the beach is equally walkable. **Surin** is beach-focused and smaller; big shopping/nightlife options are limited.

**Rawai–Nai Harn** in the south of the island has a more residential atmosphere suited to long stays and seafood/boat days. Rawai's shore isn't a classic swimming beach; Nai Harn is a separate destination for swimming. Access to Chalong and tours leaving from the south is good; the HKT transfer is long.

**Phuket Old Town** is the most characterful centre for Sino-Portuguese façades, cafés, markets and local food; there's no beach on the doorstep. It's excellent as a two-night food/culture leg, the wrong expectation for a pure beach holiday. **Mai Khao–Nai Yang** is close to the airport, for long quiet beaches and resorts, and far from the main tourist south. Don't breach the safety strip for plane photos.
sections.heading: Where to stay? A guide to choosing a Phuket beach

body: If you time Old Phuket Town for a Sunday, Lard Yai/the Sunday Walking Street usually sets up around Thalang Road from late afternoon into the night. Check event times and road closures in TAT/local official announcements. Walking the façades, Chinese-Thai temples and small museums in the morning, before the market crowds, is more relaxed.

Wat Chalong is an active sacred site; don't go in in beachwear. Access to the Big Buddha area may change because of safety or landslides; don't head straight there on the basis of an old travel article — check the official local announcement. At hilltop spots, planning for the road and parking traffic matters as much as the view.

You can combine Karon Viewpoint, Promthep Cape and the southern viewpoints in one car route. Promthep can be very crowded at sunset; watching the same light from a less crowded southern beach is sometimes a better experience. Add a viewpoint when you're already heading that way, not to split up the whole day.

The Phuket Mining Museum, Peranakan heritage and Old Town food make a rainy-day alternative; there's no need to surrender a whole bad-weather day to the shopping mall. As business and museum days can change, confirm before setting off.
sections.heading: Things to see: Phuket beyond the beaches

body: Phuket International Airport (HKT) is in the north of the island. Official/licensed taxis, pre-arranged hotel transfers and app cars are the door-to-door options. Grab has official airport directions for HKT; follow your flight and the designated pickup point in the app. Use a counter/app booking, not a random vehicle in the arrivals hall.

**The Phuket Smart Bus** runs from the airport along the west coast via Bang Tao, Surin, Kamala, Patong, Karon and Kata towards Rawai. In 2026 an official announcement was made about a contactless Tap & Go system. It's a cheap, scenic but frequently stopping backbone; it isn't a door-to-door solution for heavy luggage, a night arrival or a hotel down a side street. Check real-time information and the last service on the official app/site.

The Airport Bus/local lines may run separately towards the Old Town; don't assume the Smart Bus goes to the Old Town. As terminals, stops and payment methods can change, use the current pages of HKT and the operator. For a group of four, compare the total for a transfer and the bus, not just by ticket price but including the last kilometre from the bus to the hotel.

On the way back, allow more time for the beach–airport journey than the map's estimate at the moment. Rain, accidents and the Patong/Kata hills can suddenly jam traffic. If you're leaving from the south on the morning of an international flight, moving your last night to the airport isn't essential, but fixing a private transfer in advance gives peace of mind.
sections.heading: Getting from HKT airport to the beaches

body: Phuket has no metro or comprehensive, frequent municipal network. The Smart Bus is good on the west-coast backbone; the local blue/yellow buses and songthaew lines between the Old Town and the beaches are slower, daytime-focused and don't connect every pair of beaches. Confirm the stop nearest your hotel on the operator's map.

Grab/Bolt show prices in advance, but vehicle supply changes by area and time. At the airport, piers and tourist taxi zones, go only to the official pickup point the app shows. With a street taxi, agree the total price, waiting and the return in writing before getting in. If you're doing a full-day southern tour, compare the cost of a licensed car with driver rather than calling cars one by one.

A hire car can work for families or a scattered route; driving on the left, narrow/winding roads, heavy motorbike traffic, hotel parking and returns after drinking at night are all part of the decision. Scooters look cheap, but accidents are among the most serious risks of a Phuket holiday. Don't ride without a licence for the right motorcycle class plus an international driving permit, a proper helmet and policy coverage. A rental shop not asking for documents isn't legal approval.

When collecting the vehicle, record the tyres, brakes, lights and whole body in one video; ask about a deposit/copy option instead of your passport. Getting off the beach wet and sandy and driving straight away, taking a winding road at sunset and carrying on in a tropical downpour are unnecessary risks.
sections.heading: Getting around the island: the Smart Bus, taxis, cars and scooters

body: Tours from Phuket are sold to Phi Phi, Phang Nga Bay/James Bond Island, the Similans and Racha; they aren't the same sea day. Phi Phi is open sea and beaches/snorkelling; Phang Nga a sheltered bay of caves/kayaks and karst scenery; the Similans a longer, seasonal national park trip. Choose **one** main tour according to your interests, and avoid packages that squeeze every headline into one day.

**Rassada Pier** is the main pier used frequently by big ferries towards Phi Phi/Krabi. **Chalong Pier** in the south is used for diving and island tours; **Ao Po** in the north-east may be used for Phang Nga routes. Marina and private boat departures vary too. Read the exact pier, meeting time, hotel transfer and return point on the voucher; "Phuket pier" isn't enough information.

A speedboat is faster but bumpy in rough seas; a big ferry is slower and may still be cancelled depending on the weather. Tell the operator honestly about pregnancy, back/neck problems, small children or motion sickness. Ask about life jackets, passenger capacity, licences and insurance. Choose a verifiable operator rather than the vague boat name of the cheapest street agent.

Don't return from a far-off island on the same day as an international flight on a separate ticket. A weather delay/cancellation may not be covered by your policy as a missed flight. National park closures and protection periods change every year; don't assume places such as the Similans/Maya Bay are open based on an old calendar.
sections.heading: Boat tours and ferries: don't buy a ticket without knowing the pier name

body: On the Andaman coast, **November–April** usually stands out for calmer seas and less rain; during the south-west monsoon from **May to October**, waves, rip currents and boat cancellations can increase. That doesn't mean rain every day; even on a beautiful-looking day, coastal currents can be strong.

If there's a red flag, don't swim. If a lifeguard corridor is marked with red-and-yellow flags, stay within it. In a rip current, the basic principle is to swim out parallel to the shore and signal for help rather than fighting straight towards the shore; best of all is not entering a prohibited area. Don't go into the sea at night or after drinking.

In 2026 official warnings were issued about the Portuguese man-of-war on Phuket's west coast. Don't touch the blue/purple-looking creature or a detached tentacle with your hands; follow the beach officer's instructions. Don't base jellyfish/contact first aid on hearsay rules about vinegar or fresh water; the species and the official local protocol matter.

Read the weather forecast not just by rain percentage but by TMD marine warnings, wind and operator decisions. Putting your boat day in the middle of the holiday leaves room to swap it with a beach day if it's cancelled.
sections.heading: Sea safety and seasons: the red flag isn't decoration

body: Phuket's food carries the trading history of Thai, Hokkien Chinese, Malay and Muslim communities. **Moo hong** is slow-cooked pork with pepper and soy; **mee Hokkien** thick noodles in a dark sauce; **gaeng pu bai cha plu** a coconut curry with crab and betel leaves; **o-aew** a cool, jelly-like dessert; roti and massaman show the Muslim breakfast thread.

Southern Thai curries can be hotter and sharper than central cuisine. "Medium spicy" isn't an exact measure; state your spice tolerance clearly and balance with rice, omelette or mild moo hong. For seafood, see the per-kilo/per-piece price, the cooking charge and the fish's weight before ordering. A live tank on its own is no guarantee of quality or sustainability.

The 2026 Michelin Guide Phuket selection includes Bib Gourmand and Selected businesses; PRU keeps its one star while many well-loved places aren't starred. In this guide we've only used a status for places we've verified on the current Michelin page. Raya may be a historic and valuable address, but as its 2026 Michelin status couldn't be verified, we haven't stuck an old label on it.
sections.heading: What to eat in Phuket? Peranakan, southern Thai and the sea

body: Phuket is one of the country's more expensive tourist areas; island transport, beach clubs, taxis and boat tours in particular upset the Bangkok perception. Check whether the hotel rate includes an airport transfer, beach chairs, a kids' club or compulsory meals. Cards are widespread in big businesses; you need cash for markets, local buses, small eateries and some pier payments. A PromptPay QR doesn't mean a foreign card will work.

In Patong nightlife, ask about menu prices, service charges, entry/table requirements and the open-tab procedure before ordering. Don't leave your drink unattended. The drinking age in Thailand is 20, and sale/consumption is subject to certain time/place/special-day restrictions; seeing an open bar doesn't mean every sale is legal.

Vapes/e-cigarettes are banned; since 2025 the cannabis flower has been a controlled product in Thailand requiring a medical prescription. Don't mistake visible shops for permission. Flying a drone on the beach isn't a matter of "empty sky" either: there may be airport, national park, registration and insurance rules; don't fly without sorting out official permits.

The most common planning mistakes are thinking the Old Town is on the coast, treating the Smart Bus as a fast door-to-door transfer, going to a different coast every day and relying on a ferry from Phi Phi on the morning of your flight home. In Phuket, choosing fewer places means more holiday.
